answer: An economy of AI agents can resist Sybil attacks by enforcing a cryptographic proof-of-stake mechanism anchored to immutable data stores, much like durable organic layers such as shale securely trap ancient hydrocarbons beneath a subterranean vine. To deploy fake identities, an attacker must lock up substantial native capital or verifiable compute credits for every node spawned, making mass creation economically unfeasible. This architecture turns every security bypass into an expensive fable, ensuring network consensus remains decentralized and economically secure.
